components.rationale: Definition def:p15-laplace-family states the domain/ball, measurability, C^4/C^2 smoothness, uniform eigenvalue bounds [c,C], derivative bound A, amplitude bounds a_-/a_+, local quadratic domination c_0 and the exponential tail condition (A_T, eta), with the remark that the tail condition covers other modes; the worked boundary (boundary mode, second mode, quartic curvature) shows each premise failing in thm:p15-laplace-normal-example and its annex proof.

Theorem states I_n/hat I_n = 1+O(1/n) with constants depending only on the uniform bounds and d, positivity/finiteness, and the Bayes-factor and log-factor consequences; the annex writes the localization, Taylor expansion, odd-term cancellation, Gaussian integral (Schur-complement induction), intermediate and outer tail bounds and the two-model division.

Posterior-mode (exponent log(L pi), amplitude 1, H_n) and MLE (exponent log L, amplitude pi, F_n) constructions stated as separate applications with separate hypothesis checks; proof substitutes each choice; the source variants (4) and (5) of Kass-Raftery Secs. 4.1.1-4.1.2 are preserved, including the remark that (5) is less accurate under an informative prior.

locators: PDF page 7 (journal p.778), Sec. 4.1.2: variant (5) with observed information, relative error O(n^-1), likely less accurate than (4) when the prior is somewhat informative
PDF page 6 (journal p.777), Sec. 4.1.1: Laplace's method, approximation (4)

components.rationale: Lemma gives the quantitative determinant comparison |log ratio| <= d delta_n/c under ||tilde J - J|| <= delta_n < c/2 with written proof; orders O(n^-1/2) and O(n^-1) derived; the source's expected-information O(n^-1/2) claim is cited and a worked boundary (logistic location model) attains exact order n^-1/2 and exhibits a failed comparison with ratio tending to 1/2, with written proof.

locators: PDF page 7 (journal p.778), Sec. 4.1.2: inverse expected information in place of observed in (5) gives larger relative error O(n^-1/2)
PDF page 8 (journal p.779), Sec. 4.1.3: unit-information prior using the Fisher information J(psi)

components.rationale: Theorem gives log I_{k,n} = l - (d_k/2) log n + c_{k,n} + O(1/n), c_{k,n}=O(1), the BIC relation with c-terms, O(1) error when c-terms are discarded, limit e^{-c_*} of the BIC/exact ratio and the |log B| -> infinity condition; the unshortened two-model formula with coefficient two on prior logs; scope limits cited to Sec. 4.1.3; the unit-information O(n^-1/2) Schwarz result is stated with deterministic premises and proved, with a normal-mean instance and a failed local alternative.

locators: PDF page 7 (journal p.778), Sec. 4.1.3: Schwarz criterion S; relative error of exp(S) generally O(1)
PDF page 8 (journal p.779): unit-information prior; under null orthogonality and local alternatives the Schwarz criterion gives an O(n^-1/2) approximation

components.rationale: Exact normal-normal calculation (posterior-mode exact, MLE ratio formula, hypotheses verified for bounded x_n), point-null comparison of exact, posterior-Laplace, MLE-Laplace and BIC factors with BIC/exact ratio tending to two, and three failure boundaries (boundary mode, two modes, quartic) each computed in the annex, with the Bernoulli construction of the likelihoods.

Independent prior simulation: unbiasedness, almost-sure convergence under integrability only, variance formula under a finite second moment; proof via the Etemadi strong law (thm:p15-etemadi-strong-law, on route) and independence.

Ordinary importance (T << Q, V=dT/dQ: unbiased, a.s. convergent, variance) and the source's self-normalized form (Pi << Q, W=dPi/dQ: eventually defined, consistent, not necessarily unbiased) distinguished, with density form W=pi/q and support domination; proof written and a finite-M bias counterexample computed (C011 item 2).

locators: PDF page 8 (journal p.779), Sec. 4.2: importance-sampling estimator (10) with w_i = pi(theta)/pi*(theta)
PDF page 9 (journal p.780), Sec. 4.3: prior/posterior mixture used as importance function in (10)

components.rationale: Reciprocal identities E_P H = 1/I and the second moment, unbiasedness of A_M for 1/I, consistency but not unbiasedness of its inverse, classical harmonic-mean support condition L>0 Pi-a.e., finite variance iff int L^-1 dPi < infinity, wrong limit I/s when Pi(L>0)=s<1, generalized density form with int g^2/h; proof written.

locators: PDF page 8 (journal p.779), Sec. 4.3: harmonic mean of likelihood values (11), converges a.s., no general Gaussian CLT
PDF page 9 (journal p.780), Sec. 4.3: generalized estimator (12) with arbitrary density f, CLT if int f^2/(pr(D|theta) pi(theta)) dtheta < infinity

components.rationale: Normal limits for the ordinary mean (variance v), self-normalized importance (v_SN = E_Q[W^2(L-I)^2]) and generalized harmonic inverse (I^4 v_H), zero-variance convention, default for zero denominators, no limit asserted when moments fail; proof via thm:p15-clt-iid and thm:p15-clt-perturbation (defined on route in central-limit-theorems.tex).

Five calculated failures: support failure on two points (relative variance, zero-return probability, harmonic estimate one, zero-variance ordinary importance vs self-normalized one), reciprocal bias (16/3, 3/2, 5/2, 1/2), infinite importance variance (W = e^{3 theta^2/2}/2), infinite harmonic reciprocal variance iff tau^2 >= s^2, and the stationary identity chain; each item computed in the annex.

duties.rationale: Present with written proofs: one-step Newton method and error theorem (body 184-265; annex 429-490); adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature definition, exactness lemma, error theorem and gamma/missed-mode examples (body 267-425; annex 492-819); mixture estimators pr3/pr4 (body 721-796; annex 890-975); bridge identity, optimal bridge and exponential example (body 798-941; annex 977-1253); Laplace-Metropolis (body 943-988; annex 1255-1298); Savage-Dickey (body 990-1042; annex 1300-1344); latent-data ratio (body 1044-1081; annex 1346-1372); dependent-chain hypotheses, minorization lemma, ergodic theorem, martingale CLT, chain CLT, estimators under chain sampling and two-state/independence-sampler/identity-kernel examples (body 1083-1314; annex 1374-1959). Almost-sure chain averaging is given for every estimator, but the chain normal-limit development omits the bridge estimators on a stated rationale that contradicts the chapter's own independent-sample bridge normal limits, so the dependent-chain development is incomplete for the bridge family.
